items.title: 🚫 OpenAI has blocked a Russian network involved in operations targeting Ukraine and spreading disinformation in Latin America. The campaign aimed to discredit Ukraine, undermine support for the Armed Forces of Ukraine, and stage high-profile provocations. The operation was disguised as the “Sociological Research Center” (SRC) and led by a fictional persona named “Mia Clark.” Local employees were reportedly unaware of the network’s ties to Russia. The group used ChatGPT via VPN to draft reports and generate fake documents and audio content. OpenAI blocked the associated accounts and shared the information it had gathered with the relevant authorities.

items.title: RT by @Maks_NAFO_FELLA: 🇦🇹🇺🇦 “For the first half hour I thought we were being kidnapped”: Mykhailo Tkach recounts the details of his detention in Vienna. According to the journalist of Ukrainska Pravda, about 7 armed men in masks surrounded their car, broke the windows, and dragged him and cameraman Yaroslav Bondarenko onto the road. One of them pressed Tkach’s knee to his neck. During interrogation, Tkach was accused of espionage in the interests of Ukrainian military intelligence, participation in a criminal organization, and causing harm to Austria. After more than 12 hours of detention, Tkach was released because the suspicion of espionage was not confirmed. Cameraman Bondarenko, who was injured in the face by broken glass, was still in custody at the time of the recording. "One of the suspects we worked on could have misled the Austrian law enforcement system by providing information about cooperation with representatives of Ukrainian intelligence or the Armed Forces of Ukraine," he said.

items.title: Zelensky confirms Ukrainian strikes on the Omsk and Ukhta oil refineries. He says Ukhta, 1,900 km from Ukraine’s state border, was hit by AN-196 RS drones capable of flying around 2,500 km. The previous strike on the Omsk refinery used FP-6 drones, modified versions of the FP-1, according to Zelensky. He also confirmed a Ukrainian strike on another Russian data center, calling it a “mirror response” to Russian strikes on Ukraine. #Ukraine

items.title: Ukraine’s middle-strike campaign hit more than 30 Russian air defense, radar and EW systems, over 40 command posts and more than 50 logistics facilities in September. Targets included S-400 launchers, Buk-M3 and Pantsir systems and multiple radar types. More than 20 facilities linked to drone storage, preparation, production and operations were also hit. Other confirmed targets included a Su-24, MiG-29, Ka-27, BK-16 landing craft and Mangust patrol boat. #Ukraine

items.title: Before his detention, Rybar founder Mikhail Zvinchuk boasted that he had entered Montenegro despite sanctions and a travel ban. He claimed a border guard searched his pockets but “forgot to check the databases,” allowing him to enter. Montenegro’s PM has since confirmed his detention. #Russia
items.summary:
Before his detention, Rybar founder Mikhail Zvinchuk boasted that he had entered Montenegro despite sanctions and a travel ban. He claimed a border guard searched his pockets but “forgot to check the databases,” allowing him to enter. Montenegro’s PM has since confirmed his detention. #Russia
NOELREPORTS 🇪🇺 🇺🇦 (@NOELreports)
Montenegrin authorities detained Mikhail Zvinchuk, head of the Russian Rybar network, along with his wife Valeria and three others in Risan, Vijesti reports. Police and Montenegro’s National Security Agency are conducting an operation targeting suspected hybrid activities by the network. Vijesti says British and US authorities have linked Rybar to Kremlin propaganda and foreign influence operations, while the UK has sanctioned Zvinchuk. #Russia

items.title: Ukraine’s General Staff confirms overnight strikes on three facilities in Russia linked to missile launch systems, missile fuel and explosives. Ukrainian forces hit the Barmin Research Institute of Launch Complexes near Dalnee Konstantinovo-5, the Redkinsky Experimental Plant in Tver Oblast and an ICBM disposal center near Surovatikha. The Redkino plant produces Decilin-M fuel components used in Kh-55 and Kh-101 cruise missiles, according to the General Staff. #Ukraine

items.title: Ukrainian forces struck Lukoil’s Ukhta oil refinery in Russia’s Komi Republic, according to ASTRA’s OSINT analysis of eyewitness footage. Smoke was seen rising from the refinery grounds. The facility processes around 4-5 million tonnes of oil annually and produces gasoline and diesel. #Russia
items.summary:
Ukrainian forces struck Lukoil’s Ukhta oil refinery in Russia’s Komi Republic, according to ASTRA’s OSINT analysis of eyewitness footage. Smoke was seen rising from the refinery grounds. The facility processes around 4-5 million tonnes of oil annually and produces gasoline and diesel. #Russia
NOELREPORTS 🇪🇺 🇺🇦 (@NOELreports)
❗️An attack is being reported on Lukoil’s Ukhta oil refinery in Russia’s Komi Republic. The facility can process about 4.2 million tonnes of crude oil annually and produces gasoline, diesel, fuel oil and other petroleum products. The refinery also supplies fuel and lubricants to Russian forces, making it part of Russia’s military logistics network. The facility was previously targeted by Ukrainian long-range drones in February 2026. #Russia
